content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching a tree most commonly symbolizes a person (or a people) whose inner spiritual condition is made visible in outward 'fruit' — especially the righteous person who, rooted in God, flourishes like a well-watered tree. Closely intertwined with this is the tree as a symbol of God-given life itself, epitomized by the Tree of Life.","primary_basis":["Psalm 1:3 (the righteous like a tree planted by streams of water)","Jeremiah 17:7-8 (the one who trusts in the LORD is like a tree planted by water)","Psalm 92:12-14 (the righteous flourish like the palm tree)","Matthew 7:17-20 / Luke 6:43-44 (a tree is known by its fruit)","Matthew 3:10 (every tree not bearing good fruit is cut down)","Isaiah 61:3 (oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD)","Genesis 2:9 and Revelation 22:2 (the Tree of Life)","Proverbs 3:18; 11:30 (wisdom and the fruit of the righteous as a tree of life)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The Tree of Life as a distinct symbol of eternal life, paradise restored, and (in much Christian exegesis) Christ himself or the cross as the means of restored life.","basis":["Genesis 2:9; 3:22-24","Revelation 2:7; 22:2, 14","Proverbs 3:18"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"The cross of Christ referred to as 'the tree,' linking crucifixion to the curse of hanging on a tree and to redemption.","basis":["Acts 5:30; 10:39; 13:29","Galatians 3:13 (citing Deuteronomy 21:22-23)","1 Peter 2:24"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Great trees as symbols of kingdoms, empires, or proud rulers — exalted, sheltering many, and cut down in judgment.","basis":["Daniel 4:10-26 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree)","Ezekiel 17:22-24; 31:3-14 (Assyria/Egypt as cedars)","Judges 9:8-15 (Jotham's parable of the trees)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The fig tree (and sometimes the olive tree or vine) as a symbol of Israel, its fruitfulness or barrenness signaling covenant faithfulness or judgment.","basis":["Mark 11:12-21 / Matthew 21:18-19 (cursing of the fig tree)","Luke 13:6-9 (parable of the barren fig tree)","Hosea 9:10; Jeremiah 8:13","Romans 11:16-24 (the olive tree and grafted branches)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The mustard seed growing into a tree as a picture of the kingdom of God's growth (variously read positively as expansive growth or, in a minority reading, as abnormal/compromised growth).","basis":["Matthew 13:31-32","Mark 4:30-32","Luke 13:18-19","Ezekiel 17:23; Daniel 4:12 (birds nesting in branches as background imagery)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Trees as sites or symbols of idolatry and false worship ('under every green tree,' Asherah poles), so that the tree stands for pagan cult practice.","basis":["Deuteronomy 12:2; 16:21","1 Kings 14:23; 2 Kings 17:10","Jeremiah 2:20; 3:6; Isaiah 57:5"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Esoteric or heavily allegorized readings, e.g., the tree of the knowledge of good and evil as sexuality, or 'trees' in prophetic texts decoded as specific angelic/human figures; found in fringe or sectarian interpretation rather than mainstream scholarship.","basis":["Genesis 3 (allegorized)","Ezekiel 31 (allegorized)","Mark 8:24 ('I see men as trees, walking,' sometimes symbolically pressed)"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"'Tree' is a genuinely polyvalent biblical image, and standard reference works (e.g., dictionaries of biblical imagery) treat it under several heads rather than one fixed meaning. There is broad consensus on a cluster of recognized senses — the righteous person known by fruit, the Tree of Life, the cross, kingdoms/rulers, and Israel as fig/olive tree — but no single settled symbolic meaning covering all occurrences. Context (Genesis, Psalms/wisdom, prophets, Gospels, Revelation) determines which sense interpreters apply. Any author claiming that 'tree' carries one uniform coded meaning across Scripture would be going beyond recognizable mainstream consensus."}
